note: Cheeseburger Menu provides two Block plugins (cheeseburger_menu = the off-canvas panel, cheeseburger_menu_trigger = the button) and no central admin page (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush. All config lives on block.block.<id> config entities under settings (schema block.settings.cheeseburger_menu / block.settings.cheeseburger_menu_trigger). The panel aggregates a settings.menus sequence, each entry {id, menu_type: menu|taxonomy_vocabulary, weight, settings{max_depth, icon, title...}}, plus color/opacity settings and toggles (default_css, default_js, show_navigation, parent_menu_as_link, track_active_trail, invoke_hooks). Three alter hooks fire only when invoke_hooks is TRUE. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real block config: introspection reads back a placed block's color; execution places a cheeseburger_menu block aggregating a menu, verified against the live block.block config entity.

evals.prompt: How do I add a Cheeseburger Menu (hamburger menu) to a Drupal site? Which block(s) does the module provide and how are they related?
evals.expected_output: You place two blocks via Structure > Block layout: the 'Cheeseburger menu' block (cheeseburger_menu) which renders the off-canvas panel, and the 'Cheeseburger menu trigger' block (cheeseburger_menu_trigger) which opens/closes it. The trigger references the menu block via its block_to_trigger setting. There is no separate settings page; all configuration is in the blocks.

evals.prompt: What kinds of sources can a Cheeseburger Menu block aggregate into its panel, and where is that stored in the block configuration?
evals.expected_output: It aggregates any number of menus and/or taxonomy vocabularies into one ordered tree. Stored in the block's settings.menus sequence, each entry has menu_type ('menu' or 'taxonomy_vocabulary'), id, weight and a settings map (max_depth, initial_visibility_level, title options, icon, etc.).

evals.prompt: I want to add a CSS class to specific items in a Cheeseburger Menu programmatically. Which hook do I implement, and what setting must be enabled for it to run?
evals.expected_output: Implement hook_cheeseburger_menu_item_alter(CheeseburgerMenuItem $item) and use $item->attribute / labelAttribute / triggerAttribute addClass(). It only fires when the menu block's 'Invoke hooks' (invoke_hooks) setting is TRUE (off by default for performance). Related hooks: hook_cheeseburger_menu_alter() and hook_cheeseburger_menu_tree_manipulators_alter().

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a placed Cheeseburger Menu block with the machine id 'cbm_known'. Inspect its live configuration and report the left-side background color it is set to.
On this Drupal site, place a Cheeseburger Menu block with the machine id 'cbm_task' that aggregates the site's Main navigation menu. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A block.block.cbm_task config entity exists with plugin cheeseburger_menu and settings.menus containing at least one entry (e.g. main with menu_type 'menu'). Placeable via Block::create([...'plugin'=>'cheeseburger_menu','settings'=>['menus'=>['main'=>['id'=>'main','menu_type'=>'menu','weight'=>0,'settings'=>[]]]]])->save().

evals.prompt: I want a slide-out hamburger menu on my Drupal site showing my main navigation. Set one up (call it 'cbm_task') and switch it on.
evals.expected_output: Same verified end state as the expert variant: a placed cheeseburger_menu block 'cbm_task' aggregating at least one menu (the Main menu).
